studies.html: John joins believing Jesus is the Christ with love and obedience, then grounds eternal life in God’s testimony concerning His Son. The moral tests expose empty profession, but the letter directs confidence toward life given in the Son. An anxious reader should examine real fruits without trying to build a sinless record that can stand in place of Christ.
studies.distinction: Assurance includes evidence of grace while resting upon God’s promise, not upon flawless self-observation.
studies.question: How does the testimony about the Son in verses 9 to 12 govern the stated purpose in verse 13?

books.name: 2 John
books.intro: John joins truth and love while warning against support for teachers who deny Christ's incarnation. The identity of the elect lady is disputed. Whether a woman or a congregation is addressed, the warning concerns participation in false teaching.
books.introText: John joins truth and love while warning against support for teachers who deny Christ's incarnation. The identity of the elect lady is disputed. Whether a woman or a congregation is addressed, the warning concerns participation in false teaching.

helps.text: John writes from Ephesus, probably in the 80s or 90s, the same period as 1 John.
helps.html: John writes from Ephesus, probably in the 80s or 90s, the same period as 1 John.

helps.text: The "elect lady and her children" is most often understood as a local church and its members. Some take it as a literal woman and her family.
helps.html: The "elect lady and her children" is most often understood as a local church and its members. Some take it as a literal woman and her family.

helps.text: Truth is repeated throughout the opening of 2 John. Notice how John joins love with the truth that abides in believers rather than setting the two against each other.
helps.html: Truth is repeated throughout the opening of 2 John. Notice how John joins love with the truth that abides in believers rather than setting the two against each other.

helps.text: Walking in truth is paired with love (verses 4 to 6). Both come together in the new commandment.
helps.html: Walking in truth is paired with love (verses 4 to 6). Both come together in the new commandment.

helps.text: The warning against deceivers (verses 7 to 11) names them as those who don't confess Jesus Christ as coming in the flesh. Such are antichrist.
helps.html: The warning against deceivers (verses 7 to 11) names them as those who don't confess Jesus Christ as coming in the flesh. Such are antichrist.

helps.text: The instruction not to receive such teachers into the house or greet them is severe. It applies to those teaching damnable error, not to ordinary disagreements among brothers.
helps.html: The instruction not to receive such teachers into the house or greet them is severe. It applies to those teaching damnable error, not to ordinary disagreements among brothers.

helps.text: The closing (verses 12 to 13) shows John hopes to come in person.
helps.html: The closing (verses 12 to 13) shows John hopes to come in person.

studies.title: Love is defined by truth and obedience
studies.html: John speaks of love in truth and then relates love to walking according to God’s commandments. The letter doesn’t permit us to choose between doctrinal fidelity and kindness as though they were alternative virtues. Yet its definition also exposes a harsh profession of truth that refuses the obedience and love the truth commands.
studies.distinction: Neither pleasantness nor argumentative correctness by itself fulfills the apostolic account of love.
studies.question: How does John’s definition of love prevent it from becoming a reason to disregard Christ’s commands?

studies.title: Hospitality can become participation in false teaching
studies.html: The warning concerns deceivers who deny Christ and seek reception as teachers. Giving them support and a platform can make a host participate in their work. The passage isn’t a universal command to refuse ordinary kindness to every mistaken neighbor. Its scope is established by the described teaching and the religious reception at issue.
studies.distinction: Supporting a false teacher’s mission and speaking civilly to an unbelieving neighbor are different acts.
studies.question: Which denial identifies the deceiver, and what kind of participation does the warning oppose?

books.name: 3 John
books.intro: John commends Gaius for supporting faithful gospel workers and rebukes Diotrephes for proud opposition. The brief letter shows how hospitality can serve the truth and how a desire for prominence can injure a church.
books.introText: John commends Gaius for supporting faithful gospel workers and rebukes Diotrephes for proud opposition. The brief letter shows how hospitality can serve the truth and how a desire for prominence can injure a church.

helps.text: John writes from Ephesus around the same period as 1 and 2 John.
helps.html: John writes from Ephesus around the same period as 1 and 2 John.

helps.text: Gaius is the recipient. He is commended for walking in truth and for hospitality to brothers who came through.
helps.html: Gaius is the recipient. He is commended for walking in truth and for hospitality to brothers who came through.

helps.text: Traveling ministers had to depend on the hospitality of churches. They went out for the sake of the name, taking nothing from the Gentiles (verse 7).
helps.html: Traveling ministers had to depend on the hospitality of churches. They went out for the sake of the name, taking nothing from the Gentiles (verse 7).

helps.text: Diotrephes (verses 9 to 10) is a problem leader who loves to be first. He refuses to receive the brothers and tries to put out of the church those who would.
helps.html: Diotrephes (verses 9 to 10) is a problem leader who loves to be first. He refuses to receive the brothers and tries to put out of the church those who would.

helps.text: Demetrius (verse 12) is commended as a man with a good testimony.
helps.html: Demetrius (verse 12) is commended as a man with a good testimony.

helps.text: The closing (verses 13 to 14) shows John hopes to come in person.
helps.html: The closing (verses 13 to 14) shows John hopes to come in person.

studies.title: Supporting faithful workers is fellowship in their labor
studies.html: Gaius receives believers who go out for Christ’s name. John’s commendation makes hospitality an act of cooperation with the truth. Read this alongside 2 John’s refusal of support for deceivers. The paired letters require doctrinal judgment rather than an indiscriminate welcome or an indiscriminate suspicion of every traveling teacher.
studies.distinction: Generosity needs truth to direct it. Discernment needs love to keep it from becoming a reason never to help.
studies.question: What difference in the teachers' message explains the different directions given in 2 John and 3 John?

studies.title: A church office does not sanctify a desire for prominence
studies.html: Diotrephes opposes the apostolic workers, speaks maliciously, and excludes people who receive them. His desire to be first explains the conduct. The letter exposes a misuse of church authority from within the church rather than directing believers to despise all authority. Demetrius supplies the contrast of a good testimony measured by the truth.
studies.distinction: Respect for Christ’s order isn’t a duty to endorse an officer’s malicious or self-serving acts.
studies.question: Which observable actions show that the desire for preeminence is more than an uncharitable guess about a hidden motive?

books.name: Jude
books.intro: Jude calls the church to contend for the faith against teachers who turn grace into license. Examples of judgment show the seriousness of their rebellion. The closing exhortation combines vigilance with mercy toward those in danger.
books.introText: Jude calls the church to contend for the faith against teachers who turn grace into license. Examples of judgment show the seriousness of their rebellion. The closing exhortation combines vigilance with mercy toward those in danger.

helps.text: Jude writes probably in the 60s or 70s. The exact date is uncertain.
helps.html: Jude writes probably in the 60s or 70s. The exact date is uncertain.

helps.text: The opening (verses 1 to 4) calls believers to contend for the faith once for all delivered to the saints.
helps.html: The opening (verses 1 to 4) calls believers to contend for the faith once for all delivered to the saints.

helps.text: The false teachers (verses 4 to 16) are described severely. They turn grace into license and deny the Lord.
helps.html: The false teachers (verses 4 to 16) are described severely. They turn grace into license and deny the Lord.

helps.text: Old Testament examples of judgment (verses 5 to 7) include the wilderness generation, the angels who left their habitation, and Sodom and Gomorrah.
helps.html: Old Testament examples of judgment (verses 5 to 7) include the wilderness generation, the angels who left their habitation, and Sodom and Gomorrah.

helps.text: Jude 14 to 15 contains words also found in 1 Enoch. The inspired citation establishes the truth of what Jude affirms, not the canonical authority of the whole source. Compare Paul's use of pagan poets in Acts 17.28.
helps.html: Jude 14 to 15 contains words also found in 1 Enoch. The inspired citation establishes the truth of what Jude affirms, not the canonical authority of the whole source. Compare Paul's use of pagan poets in Acts 17.28.

helps.text: Jude 9 refers to Michael's dispute with the devil over Moses' body. Related traditions circulated outside Scripture, but Jude doesn't identify a written source. Don't claim certainty about a source the text doesn't name.
helps.html: Jude 9 refers to Michael's dispute with the devil over Moses' body. Related traditions circulated outside Scripture, but Jude doesn't identify a written source. Don't claim certainty about a source the text doesn't name.

helps.text: The pastoral exhortations (verses 17 to 23) call believers to build themselves up, to keep themselves in God’s love, and to show mercy with fear, snatching others from the fire.
helps.html: The pastoral exhortations (verses 17 to 23) call believers to build themselves up, to keep themselves in God’s love, and to show mercy with fear, snatching others from the fire.

studies.title: An inspired citation does not canonize a whole source
studies.html: Jude cites a prophecy also found in 1 Enoch. The words Jude affirms belong to inspired Scripture because of his inspired use. That doesn’t establish the authority of every other claim in the work in which similar words occur. Paul likewise uses material outside the canon. Distinguish the truth affirmed in the canonical passage from an endorsement of an entire surrounding source.
studies.distinction: A truthful borrowed statement doesn’t make every statement by its earlier transmitter divinely inspired.
studies.question: What exactly does Jude affirm, and which broader claim about 1 Enoch would exceed his citation?

studies.title: God’s keeping and the command to keep yourselves belong together
studies.html: Jude commands believers to build themselves up, pray, and keep themselves in God’s love, then praises the One able to keep them from falling. The command names active perseverance through appointed means. The doxology locates its sustaining power in God. Neither the duty nor the promise should be removed to make the other seem simpler.
studies.distinction: Dependence upon preserving grace does not turn perseverance into inactivity.
studies.question: How do the commanded activities and the closing doxology describe different aspects of the same persevering life?

books.name: Revelation
books.intro: John receives visions of the risen Christ and His rule over the church and the nations. The book addresses real congregations through apocalyptic imagery rooted in the Old Testament. Its promised end is Christ's victory and God's dwelling with His people.
books.introText: John receives visions of the risen Christ and His rule over the church and the nations. The book addresses real congregations through apocalyptic imagery rooted in the Old Testament. Its promised end is Christ's victory and God's dwelling with His people.

helps.text: Most amillennialists read Revelation in cycles that recapitulate the same period from different angles, each showing the same age from a different vantage.
helps.html: Most amillennialists read Revelation in cycles that recapitulate the same period from different angles, each showing the same age from a different vantage.

helps.text: John writes from Patmos in exile, probably during the reign of Domitian around AD 95.
helps.html: John writes from Patmos in exile, probably during the reign of Domitian around AD 95.

helps.text: The opening vision of Christ (chapter 1) sets the tone. John receives the vision in the Spirit on the Lord’s Day (1.10), the new covenant name for the first day of the week, the day of the resurrection. He sees the risen Christ, the Alpha and the Omega, the first and the last, the living one. Read this chapter slowly.
helps.html: The opening vision of Christ (chapter 1) sets the tone. John receives the vision in the Spirit on the Lord’s Day (1.10), the new covenant name for the first day of the week, the day of the resurrection. He sees the risen Christ, the Alpha and the Omega, the first and the last, the living one. Read this chapter slowly.

helps.text: Read each message in chapters 2 to 3 individually. Smyrna and Philadelphia receive no rebuke, and Laodicea receives no commendation. Christ knows the distinct condition of every congregation.
helps.html: Read each message in chapters 2 to 3 individually. Smyrna and Philadelphia receive no rebuke, and Laodicea receives no commendation. Christ knows the distinct condition of every congregation.

helps.text: The throne room visions (chapters 4 to 5) center the book. The Lamb who was slain is the only one worthy to open the scroll.
helps.html: The throne room visions (chapters 4 to 5) center the book. The Lamb who was slain is the only one worthy to open the scroll.

helps.text: The seals, trumpets, and bowls repeatedly bring us to scenes of judgment. Many amillennial interpreters understand these as overlapping cycles. Trace the textual reasons for that reading instead of treating the arrangement as an undisputed fact.
helps.html: The seals, trumpets, and bowls repeatedly bring us to scenes of judgment. Many amillennial interpreters understand these as overlapping cycles. Trace the textual reasons for that reading instead of treating the arrangement as an undisputed fact.

helps.text: The dragon, the beast, and the false prophet (chapters 12 to 14) form the unholy triad opposed to God, His Christ, and His church.
helps.html: The dragon, the beast, and the false prophet (chapters 12 to 14) form the unholy triad opposed to God, His Christ, and His church.

helps.text: The fall of Babylon (chapters 17 to 18) celebrates the judgment of the great harlot. The imagery draws on Old Testament Babylon and Tyre.
helps.html: The fall of Babylon (chapters 17 to 18) celebrates the judgment of the great harlot. The imagery draws on Old Testament Babylon and Tyre.

helps.text: The rider on the white horse (chapter 19) is the second coming of Christ. He treads the winepress of the wrath of God.
helps.html: The rider on the white horse (chapter 19) is the second coming of Christ. He treads the winepress of the wrath of God.

helps.text: This guide reads Revelation 20 amillennially. Christ presently reigns, the departed saints live and reign with Him, and Satan's final assault ends in judgment. The bodily resurrection and final judgment are certain. WCF 32 and WCF 33 confess those truths without prescribing every detail of millennial chronology. Reformed Presbyterian postmillennial interpretations also exist. Test the exposition against the passage without treating that difference as a different gospel.
helps.html: This guide reads Revelation 20 amillennially. Christ presently reigns, the departed saints live and reign with Him, and Satan's final assault ends in judgment. The bodily resurrection and final judgment are certain. WCF 32 and WCF 33 confess those truths without prescribing every detail of millennial chronology. Reformed Presbyterian postmillennial interpretations also exist. Test the exposition against the passage without treating that difference as a different gospel.

helps.text: The new heaven and new earth (chapters 21 to 22) is the consummation. The new Jerusalem comes down. God dwells with His people. There's no more death, no more pain. The Lamb is the lamp. The book closes with the promise "I come quickly" (22.20).

studies.title: A symbol’s explanation governs its use
studies.html: John describes the vision and receives an interpretation of its stars and lampstands. Those identifications provide a model of restraint. Begin with meanings supplied by the book and its scriptural background rather than a visual resemblance to modern objects. The vision also concerns actual churches whose conduct is addressed in the following messages. Symbolism doesn’t detach the book from historical hearers.
studies.distinction: A revealed symbolic meaning has greater authority than an imaginative identification based on appearance alone.
studies.question: Which symbols are explicitly identified, and how does that explanation direct the reading of chapters 2 to 3?

studies.title: The final inheritance is life with God in a renewed creation
studies.html: The city and marriage imagery portray the consummated dwelling of God with His redeemed people. The absence of death and sorrow concerns their actual final condition, not merely a change of political administration. Read the symbols with the clear promise of resurrection and final judgment. Present experiences of grace anticipate this inheritance without exhausting it.
studies.distinction: An inaugurated kingdom and present spiritual comfort don’t mean that the promised end of death has already fully arrived.
studies.question: Which features of the promised condition prevent reducing the whole passage to an event already completed within ordinary history?

gospel.title: The God who saves
gospel.html:
God made us, and we owe Him our worship and obedience. He is eternal, holy, and unchanging. There is one God in three Persons, the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit. The Persons are distinct, yet each is fully God. They share one divine being and one will.

God's holiness means He cannot approve of evil. His mercy means sinners have reason to come to Him. These aren't competing parts of His character. At the cross, He saves His people without setting His justice aside. Salvation begins in His eternal purpose of grace, not in anything He foresaw in us.

gospel.title: Our need
gospel.html:
God made Adam upright and placed him under a covenant requiring perfect obedience. Adam disobeyed as the representative head of mankind. All who descend from him by ordinary generation inherit his guilt and a corrupted nature. Christ alone was conceived without sin.

We also commit sins of our own. We break God's law because our hearts are turned from Him. Being spiritually dead doesn't mean we're incapable of thought or choice. It means we won't turn to God in saving faith unless His Spirit makes us alive. We need forgiveness and a new heart. Neither can be earned.

gospel.title: The person of Christ
gospel.html:
Jesus Christ is the eternal Son of God who took a true human nature to Himself. He was conceived by the Holy Ghost and born of the virgin Mary. He is one Person, fully God and fully man. His two natures are neither mixed nor divided.

He obeyed the law His people had broken. His whole life was righteous, and His death was willing obedience to His Father. We need more than the removal of our guilt. We need the righteousness that Christ alone supplies. God counts His obedience and satisfaction to believers, who receive Him through faith alone.

gospel.title: His death and resurrection
gospel.html:
Christ died as the substitute for His people. He bore the judgment their sins deserved and fully satisfied God's justice. His suffering included the anguish of bearing divine wrath, not only the pain inflicted by men.

His cry of forsakenness must be taken seriously. He was deprived of the comforting sense of His Father's presence as He bore the curse. Yet the Trinity was never divided, the Father never ceased loving the Son, and Christ's divine and human natures remained united. His sufferings were real, and His trust in His Father did not fail.

On the third day He rose bodily from the dead. He later ascended into heaven, where He reigns and intercedes for His people. His resurrection confirms the victory of His finished work. He will return bodily to raise the dead and judge the world.

gospel.title: How sinners receive Him
gospel.html:
God commands everyone who hears the gospel to repent and believe in Jesus Christ. You don't have to discover whether you're elect before coming to Him. His command and promise give you warrant to come.

Saving faith receives and rests upon Christ alone for salvation. Repentance is a turning from sin to God, with grief for sin and a purpose to walk in obedience. Neither is a payment for mercy. Both are gifts of God's grace, and neither should be confused with merely knowing religious facts or feeling afraid of judgment.

In effectual calling, the Spirit renews the sinner and brings him willingly to Christ. Regeneration is the source of faith, not its reward. God justifies the believer through faith alone, on the basis of Christ's righteousness. Faith doesn't merit acceptance. It receives the Savior who has secured it.

If you haven't trusted Christ, come to Him. Your sin is a reason you need Him. Don't make waiting until you feel worthy an excuse for refusing His mercy.

gospel.title: Life with Christ
gospel.html:
Everyone united to Christ is justified and adopted into God's family. Justification changes our standing before God. Sanctification changes us inwardly as the Spirit teaches us to hate sin and walk in obedience. These blessings belong together, but they aren't the same thing.

We obey because God has received us in Christ. Our obedience contributes nothing to the righteousness by which we're justified. It is nevertheless necessary as the fruit of living faith. Repentance continues throughout the Christian life because sin remains in us.

God ordinarily strengthens His people through His Word, the sacraments, and prayer. Read your Bible and belong to a faithful church. Receive the ministry Christ has appointed rather than measuring spiritual health by the strength of an experience.

Christians suffer, and some endure long seasons of darkness. Their suffering isn't God's condemning wrath. A Father's discipline may correct particular sins, but we shouldn't assume every illness or loss can be traced to a particular offense. Job warns against that judgment.

God preserves His people in faith. He uses warnings, correction, and the help of other believers to keep them. Assurance can weaken, but Christ doesn't become a weaker Savior when our confidence falters. Look first to His promises. Then consider the imperfect but real fruits of His Spirit without making them the foundation of your acceptance.

gospel.title: Our hope
gospel.html:
At death, believers' souls are made perfect in holiness and received into God's presence. Their bodies remain united to Christ and await the resurrection. When He returns, He will raise them in glory. They will enjoy Him forever, free from sin and suffering.

These reading helps serve that life of faith. They can't save anyone or replace the Bible. Use them to understand what God has said and to follow Christ more faithfully. If a help is mistaken, Scripture must correct it.

library.Foreword:
I wrote these helps for believers who want to understand their Bibles more faithfully. The Lord brought me to faith while I was reading Matthew. I know what it is to open the Scriptures with questions I couldn't yet answer.

This guide follows the Reformed faith expressed in the Westminster Standards. It states those convictions plainly, including where Christians disagree. Agreement with every conclusion here isn't the ground of anyone's salvation. Christ alone saves, and every teacher remains subject to His Word.

Use the helps with your Bible open. Bring difficult questions to faithful elders and keep testing what you read. My hope is that these pages help you attend more closely to what God has actually said.
library.Preface:
This companion is for readers beginning to study Scripture and for those ready to work more closely with its doctrine. Its starting point is the same at every level. God’s Word has a true meaning that we are to receive, not remake.

The short helps let you begin without a long preliminary course. The further studies and lessons explain the reasons behind the guidance. They distinguish the literal sense from a flat reading, necessary inference from suggestion, and faithful application from an imported message.

The theology follows the Westminster Standards and the Reformed Presbyterian convictions stated in the guide. Scripture remains the final judge. The aim of going deeper is a better understanding of the Word God has given, joined to faith and obedience, rather than the discovery of meanings no one could test.
library.How to Use This Guide:
Begin with the biblical passage and its book overview. The reading helps draw attention to its setting and argument. When you want fuller work, open the further studies at the end of each guide. Each study connects an actual passage with doctrine and gives a question to work through.

The Study guide contains 24 lessons, including four extended close readings. Start with Foundations if you’re new to interpretation. Continue through the kinds of writing and doctrinal connections as questions arise. The worked examples show the method on specific passages, with KJV context available beside them.

The doctrine index connects subjects to studies across the Bible. Use it to compare related passages without making a collection of references replace each passage’s own argument. The glossary explains unfamiliar terms, and selected entries link to a fuller lesson.

Your reviewed guides, completed lessons, practiced passages, and reading position remain in this browser. Export a reading record from Your reading to keep a backup or carry it to another device. These markers record study, not spiritual maturity.
library.Closing Word:
Keep reading the Bible itself. These helps have served their purpose when they lead you back to the passage with greater understanding and a heart more willing to obey.

You won't settle every difficulty at once. Ask for help, return to the clearer teaching of Scripture, and be willing to correct a mistaken reading. Growth in understanding ordinarily comes through patient use of the means God has given.

Above all, rest in Christ. Your skill as a reader isn't the ground of your acceptance with God. He receives His people in His Son and teaches them as His children.
library.Recommended Reading:
Choose a resource to answer the question you actually have. You don't need a large collection to begin. Check the passage before consulting notes, and distinguish a writer's strengths from agreement with all his theology.

Begin here

The Westminster Confession and Catechisms provide the doctrinal framework of this guide. G. I. Williamson's study guide can help you work through the Confession. Louis Berkhof's Summary of Christian Doctrine offers a short introduction to Reformed theology.

For a passage you're studying

Matthew Henry is useful for devotional exposition. Calvin often follows the argument of a passage closely. The Let's Study series offers accessible studies of individual books. Spurgeon's Treasury of David is devoted to the Psalms.

For the Christian life

Richard Sibbes's The Bruised Reed treats Christ's care for weak believers. Thomas Watson's The Doctrine of Repentance explains repentance practically. John Owen's The Mortification of Sin addresses putting remaining sin to death by the Spirit.

For salvation and assurance

John Murray's Redemption Accomplished and Applied distinguishes Christ's finished work from its application. William Guthrie's The Christian's Great Interest addresses assurance and the call to come to Christ.

Use recommendations with judgment

A useful book can contain errors. In particular, Calvinistic authors may differ from Westminster on baptism, worship, or the last things. Read those differences openly rather than treating Reformed as a guarantee that every note agrees with this guide.
library.On Memorizing Scripture:
Choose a short passage you understand. Read its surrounding paragraph before beginning. Say the words aloud, then hide the text and try to recall them. Check your wording against the passage rather than guessing.

Review yesterday's passage before learning another. A few minutes of regular attention is better than an ambitious plan you can't maintain. Longer passages can be learned a sentence at a time while you keep the whole argument in view.

Think about what the words teach and bring them into prayer. The practiced marker records a review, not proof that a passage has been mastered. Return to familiar passages so their wording and meaning remain clear.
library.About the Author:
My name is Colt. I'm a husband, a father, and a custodian. I'm not a pastor. The Lord brought me to faith in 2025 while I was reading the Gospel according to St Matthew after many years of unbelief.

The Christian life since then has included hard trials as well as joy. I've needed the same grace I commend in these pages. My hope rests in Christ, not in how much I've learned or how well I've lived.

I write as a communicant member of a Reformed Presbyterian church who wants to help other believers read their Bibles. This revised companion should be tested by Scripture and used alongside the teaching ministry of a faithful local church. Bring questions about its teaching to your elders.

glossary.text: The conviction that the inspired writings of God are now complete in the sixty-six books of the Old and New Testaments. No further inspired writings are to be expected. The Spirit illumines what is already written and doesn't contradict it. WCF 1.1.

glossary.definition: The reading of any passage in light of the whole Bible, since the Bible is one book with one divine Author. The canonical context is the final and decisive context for interpretation.
glossary.text: The reading of any passage in light of the whole Bible, since the Bible is one book with one divine Author. The canonical context is the final and decisive context for interpretation.

glossary.definition: A summary of Christian doctrine in the form of questions and answers, used for teaching and learning. The Westminster Larger and Shorter Catechisms are the standard catechisms of the Reformed Presbyterian tradition.
glossary.text: A summary of Christian doctrine in the form of questions and answers, used for teaching and learning. The Westminster Larger and Shorter Catechisms are the standard catechisms of the Reformed Presbyterian tradition.

glossary.definition: The portion of the Mosaic law dealing with sacrifices, the priesthood, the temple, dietary rules, and ritual purity. The ceremonial law was fulfilled in Christ and is no longer binding on the church. WCF 19.3.
glossary.text: The portion of the Mosaic law dealing with sacrifices, the priesthood, the temple, dietary rules, and ritual purity. The ceremonial law was fulfilled in Christ and is no longer binding on the church. WCF 19.3.

glossary.definition: The conviction that the extraordinary revelatory gifts associated with the foundation of the church have ceased. WCF 1.1 affirms the cessation of the former ways of revealing God's will. This doesn't mean that God has ceased answering prayer, healing, or acting extraordinarily in providence.
glossary.text: The conviction that the extraordinary revelatory gifts associated with the foundation of the church have ceased. WCF 1.1 affirms the cessation of the former ways of revealing God's will. This doesn't mean that God has ceased answering prayer, healing, or acting extraordinarily in providence.

glossary.definition: The pattern Christ ordained for the church to deal with sin among its members. Private appeal first, then witnesses, then the church. The aim is restoration. The final step, when the offender won't repent, is to put the unrepentant out of the fellowship for the sake of the soul and the purity of the body. Matthew 18, 1 Corinthians 5, WCF 30.
glossary.text: The pattern Christ ordained for the church to deal with sin among its members. Private appeal first, then witnesses, then the church. The aim is restoration. The final step, when the offender won't repent, is to put the unrepentant out of the fellowship for the sake of the soul and the purity of the body. Matthew 18, 1 Corinthians 5, WCF 30.

glossary.definition: The pattern of governing the church given in the New Testament. The Reformed Presbyterian tradition holds that Christ has appointed elders (teaching and ruling) and deacons to lead and serve the church, and that elders rule together in graded courts (session, presbytery, general assembly). 1 Timothy 3, Acts 15, WCF 30 to 31.
glossary.text: The pattern of governing the church given in the New Testament. The Reformed Presbyterian tradition holds that Christ has appointed elders (teaching and ruling) and deacons to lead and serve the church, and that elders rule together in graded courts (session, presbytery, general assembly). 1 Timothy 3, Acts 15, WCF 30 to 31.

Because Christ is one Person in two natures, Scripture can speak of that Person in terms appropriate to either nature. The natures remain distinct. His human suffering does not make deity mortal, and His deity does not make His humanity unreal. WCF 8.2 and 8.7.
glossary.definition: Because Christ is one Person in two natures, Scripture can speak of that Person in terms appropriate to either nature. The natures remain distinct. His human suffering does not make deity mortal, and His deity does not make His humanity unreal. WCF 8.2 and 8.7.
A formal summary of Christian doctrine adopted by a church or assembly. The Westminster Confession of Faith (1647) is the standard confession of the Reformed Presbyterian tradition.
glossary.text: A formal summary of Christian doctrine adopted by a church or assembly. The Westminster Confession of Faith (1647) is the standard confession of the Reformed Presbyterian tradition.

glossary.definition: A formal binding relationship between two parties, often including promises, conditions, and signs. The Bible is structured by the covenants God has made with His people. WCF 7.
glossary.text: A formal binding relationship between two parties, often including promises, conditions, and signs. The Bible is structured by the covenants God has made with His people. WCF 7.

glossary.definition: God's gracious provision of life and salvation through Jesus Christ, received by faith. It's administered through the Old and New Testaments, with Christ as its substance. Distinguish its saving administration from covenants, such as the Noahic covenant, that also preserve the setting in which redemption unfolds. WCF 7.
glossary.text: God's gracious provision of life and salvation through Jesus Christ, received by faith. It's administered through the Old and New Testaments, with Christ as its substance. Distinguish its saving administration from covenants, such as the Noahic covenant, that also preserve the setting in which redemption unfolds. WCF 7.

glossary.definition: The covenant God made with Adam in the garden, by which life was promised on condition of perfect obedience and death threatened upon breach. Adam broke the covenant of works in the fall. Christ, the second Adam, kept it for His people. WCF 7.2.
glossary.text: The covenant God made with Adam in the garden, by which life was promised on condition of perfect obedience and death threatened upon breach. Adam broke the covenant of works in the fall. Christ, the second Adam, kept it for His people. WCF 7.2.

glossary.definition: An outward token appointed by God to mark the covenant. Circumcision was the sign of the old covenant. Baptism is the sign of the new.
glossary.text: An outward token appointed by God to mark the covenant. Circumcision was the sign of the old covenant. Baptism is the sign of the new.

Definitive sanctification concerns the decisive breach with sin’s dominion in union with Christ. Progressive sanctification concerns continuing growth in holiness. Neither means remaining sin is absent before glory. Romans 6; WCF 13.
glossary.definition: Definitive sanctification concerns the decisive breach with sin’s dominion in union with Christ. Progressive sanctification concerns continuing growth in holiness. Neither means remaining sin is absent before glory. Romans 6; WCF 13.

glossary.text: God is not subject to involuntary change or suffering caused by creatures. His love, mercy, and opposition to evil are fully real and perfect. The incarnate Son truly suffers according to His human nature. WCF 2.1 and 8.2.
glossary.definition: God is not subject to involuntary change or suffering caused by creatures. His love, mercy, and opposition to evil are fully real and perfect. The incarnate Son truly suffers according to His human nature. WCF 2.1 and 8.2.

glossary.text: Reading a preferred idea into a passage rather than deriving it from what the passage teaches. A true doctrine can still be wrongly imposed upon a text that is addressing another subject.
glossary.definition: Reading a preferred idea into a passage rather than deriving it from what the passage teaches. A true doctrine can still be wrongly imposed upon a text that is addressing another subject.

God’s eternal choice of certain persons in Christ to be saved, made before the foundation of the world, not on the basis of any foreseen faith or good in them, but according to His own sovereign good pleasure. WCF 3.
glossary.text: God’s eternal choice of certain persons in Christ to be saved, made before the foundation of the world, not on the basis of any foreseen faith or good in them, but according to His own sovereign good pleasure. WCF 3.

glossary.definition: The study of last things. The return of Christ, the resurrection of the dead, the final judgment, and the new heavens and new earth.
glossary.text: The study of last things. The return of Christ, the resurrection of the dead, the final judgment, and the new heavens and new earth.
Drawing the meaning from a text by attending to its words, argument, and setting. A faithful explanation should be able to show where the passage establishes its conclusion.
glossary.definition: Drawing the meaning from a text by attending to its words, argument, and setting. A faithful explanation should be able to show where the passage establishes its conclusion.

The teaching that Adam stood as the legal head of the whole human race in the covenant of works, so that his fall was the fall of all in him. Christ stands as the legal head of His people in the covenant of grace, so that His obedience and death are reckoned to all in Him. Romans 5.
glossary.text: The teaching that Adam stood as the legal head of the whole human race in the covenant of works, so that his fall was the fall of all in him. Christ stands as the legal head of His people in the covenant of grace, so that His obedience and death are reckoned to all in Him. Romans 5.

glossary.definition: The justice expressed in Israel's judicial laws that remains obligatory after the expiration of those laws with Israel as a body politic. Determining its application requires attention to the law's purpose and the rest of Scripture. WCF 19.4.
glossary.text: The justice expressed in Israel's judicial laws that remains obligatory after the expiration of those laws with Israel as a body politic. Determining its application requires attention to the law's purpose and the rest of Scripture. WCF 19.4.

glossary.definition: God’s revealing of Himself in creation, providence, and the conscience of every man. General revelation shows that God is and that He is to be feared, but it doesn't show how a sinner can be saved. Romans 1.
glossary.text: God’s revealing of Himself in creation, providence, and the conscience of every man. General revelation shows that God is and that He is to be feared, but it doesn't show how a sinner can be saved. Romans 1.

glossary.definition: The kind of literature a passage belongs to. Narrative, poetry, prophecy, parable, apocalyptic, epistle. Reading well requires knowing the genre and reading it accordingly.
glossary.text: The kind of literature a passage belongs to. Narrative, poetry, prophecy, parable, apocalyptic, epistle. Reading well requires knowing the genre and reading it accordingly.

glossary.definition: The completion of the believer's salvation in glory. At death, the soul is made perfect in holiness and received into God's presence. The body awaits its resurrection in glory at Christ's return. WCF 32 and WLC 86 to 90.
glossary.text: The completion of the believer's salvation in glory. At death, the soul is made perfect in holiness and received into God's presence. The body awaits its resurrection in glory at Christ's return. WCF 32 and WLC 86 to 90.
A conclusion that is required by what Scripture teaches, even when it is not expressed in one identical sentence. It is stronger than a plausible association or a possible application. WCF 1.6.
glossary.definition: A conclusion that is required by what Scripture teaches, even when it is not expressed in one identical sentence. It is stronger than a plausible association or a possible application. WCF 1.6.

The science and art of interpreting Scripture. The historic Reformed hermeneutic reads the Bible literally (in the intended sense of the author), grammatically, historically, and in light of the analogy of faith.
glossary.text: The science and art of interpreting Scripture. The historic Reformed hermeneutic reads the Bible literally (in the intended sense of the author), grammatically, historically, and in light of the analogy of faith.

glossary.definition: The Reformed approach to reading Scripture that seeks the intended meaning of the author by attending to the historical setting, the grammar of the text, and the canonical context. It rejects allegorical readings that ignore authorial intent.
glossary.text: The Reformed approach to reading Scripture that seeks the intended meaning of the author by attending to the historical setting, the grammar of the text, and the canonical context. It rejects allegorical readings that ignore authorial intent.

glossary.definition: The work of the Holy Spirit by which He opens the believer’s mind and heart to understand and receive the truth of Scripture. Illumination isn't new revelation. It's the Spirit applying what is already written.
glossary.text: The work of the Holy Spirit by which He opens the believer’s mind and heart to understand and receive the truth of Scripture. Illumination isn't new revelation. It's the Spirit applying what is already written.

Revelation makes God’s truth known with divine authority. Illumination is the Spirit’s work enabling us to understand and receive the revealed Word. A believer’s experience of insight does not create new canonical truth.
glossary.definition: Revelation makes God’s truth known with divine authority. Illumination is the Spirit’s work enabling us to understand and receive the revealed Word. A believer’s experience of insight does not create new canonical truth.
The legal accounting by which the sins of believers were counted to Christ at the cross and the righteousness of Christ is counted to believers by faith.
glossary.text: The legal accounting by which the sins of believers were counted to Christ at the cross and the righteousness of Christ is counted to believers by faith.

glossary.definition: The doctrine that the Bible, in its original manuscripts, is without error in everything it teaches, including history, science, ethics, and theology.
glossary.text: The doctrine that the Bible, in its original manuscripts, is without error in everything it teaches, including history, science, ethics, and theology.

glossary.definition: The act of the Holy Spirit by which the human authors of Scripture wrote what God intended them to write, so that every word of the Bible is at once their word and the very Word of God. WCF 1.2.
glossary.text: The act of the Holy Spirit by which the human authors of Scripture wrote what God intended them to write, so that every word of the Bible is at once their word and the very Word of God. WCF 1.2.

glossary.definition: The whole number of the elect, known fully only to God, gathered into one body under Christ as their Head. The invisible church is the company of all true believers across all ages. WCF 25.1.
glossary.text: The whole number of the elect, known fully only to God, gathered into one body under Christ as their Head. The invisible church is the company of all true believers across all ages. WCF 25.1.

glossary.definition: The civil laws given to Israel as a particular body politic. Those laws expired with that polity, except for the general equity that remains obligatory. WCF 19.4.
glossary.text: The civil laws given to Israel as a particular body politic. Those laws expired with that polity, except for the general equity that remains obligatory. WCF 19.4.

glossary.definition: The legal act by which God declares a sinner righteous in His sight on the basis of the imputed righteousness of Christ, received by faith alone. WCF 11.
glossary.text: The legal act by which God declares a sinner righteous in His sight on the basis of the imputed righteousness of Christ, received by faith alone. WCF 11.

The meaning conveyed by the inspired text according to its language and literary purpose. It includes intended figures of speech. It is not a rule that every word must name a physical object. WCF 1.9.
glossary.definition: The meaning conveyed by the inspired text according to its language and literary purpose. It includes intended figures of speech. It is not a rule that every word must name a physical object. WCF 1.9.

The first day of the week, the day of Christ’s resurrection, kept by the church as the Christian Sabbath. The fourth commandment’s call to a weekly Sabbath rest continues under the new covenant on the day the Lord rose. The Lord’s Day is set apart for rest, public worship, and works of necessity and mercy. WCF 21.7 to 8.
glossary.text: The first day of the week, the day of Christ’s resurrection, kept by the church as the Christian Sabbath. The fourth commandment’s call to a weekly Sabbath rest continues under the new covenant on the day the Lord rose. The Lord’s Day is set apart for rest, public worship, and works of necessity and mercy. WCF 21.7 to 8.

glossary.definition: The sacrament in which Christ gives bread and wine as signs and seals of His body and blood. Worthy receivers truly feed on Christ spiritually by faith, not by a bodily change in the elements. It remembers His finished sacrifice and nourishes His people. WCF 29.
glossary.text: The sacrament in which Christ gives bread and wine as signs and seals of His body and blood. Worthy receivers truly feed on Christ spiritually by faith, not by a bodily change in the elements. It remembers His finished sacrifice and nourishes His people. WCF 29.

glossary.definition: The ordinary instruments by which the Spirit works grace in the lives of believers. The Word read and preached, the sacraments, and prayer. Westminster Shorter Catechism Q. 88.
glossary.text: The ordinary instruments by which the Spirit works grace in the lives of believers. The Word read and preached, the sacraments, and prayer. Westminster Shorter Catechism Q. 88.

glossary.definition: The summary of God’s eternal moral will, given on stone in the Ten Commandments. The moral law continues to bind every man, believer and unbeliever alike. WCF 19.5.
glossary.text: The summary of God’s eternal moral will, given on stone in the Ten Commandments. The moral law continues to bind every man, believer and unbeliever alike. WCF 19.5.

glossary.definition: The active putting to death of remaining sin in the believer’s life by the power of the Holy Spirit. The Puritans wrote much on this duty.
glossary.text: The active putting to death of remaining sin in the believer’s life by the power of the Holy Spirit. The Puritans wrote much on this duty.

glossary.definition: The covenant of grace in its fullness, ratified by the blood of Christ, written on the heart by the Spirit, and extended to all nations. Jeremiah 31, Hebrews 8 to 10.
glossary.text: The covenant of grace in its fullness, ratified by the blood of Christ, written on the heart by the Spirit, and extended to all nations. Jeremiah 31, Hebrews 8 to 10.

glossary.definition: In one sense, all the administrations of the covenant of grace before Christ. In another sense, the Mosaic administration in particular, which has been fulfilled and surpassed in Christ. WCF 7.5 to 6.
glossary.text: In one sense, all the administrations of the covenant of grace before Christ. In another sense, the Mosaic administration in particular, which has been fulfilled and surpassed in Christ. WCF 7.5 to 6.

glossary.definition: The Word, sacraments, and prayer appointed by God for communicating the benefits of redemption. We should use them in faith while remembering that God is free to work beyond them. Their use doesn't make grace automatic. WSC 88.
glossary.text: The Word, sacraments, and prayer appointed by God for communicating the benefits of redemption. We should use them in faith while remembering that God is free to work beyond them. Their use doesn't make grace automatic. WSC 88.

glossary.definition: The doctrine that those who are truly united to Christ will persevere in faith and obedience to the end and be saved. The same God who began the work in them will finish it. WCF 17.
glossary.text: The doctrine that those who are truly united to Christ will persevere in faith and obedience to the end and be saved. The same God who began the work in them will finish it. WCF 17.

glossary.definition: The view that Christ will return after a long period of gospel triumph in the world, during which the kingdom of Christ visibly advances and many are converted. One of the historic Reformed views.
glossary.text: The view that Christ will return after a long period of gospel triumph in the world, during which the kingdom of Christ visibly advances and many are converted. One of the historic Reformed views.

glossary.definition: The interpretation that Christ returns before a future earthly millennium. This companion teaches an amillennial reading. Dispensational premillennialism's separation of Israel and the church conflicts with the unity of the covenant of grace confessed in WCF 7.5 and WCF 7.6. The Westminster Standards don't name a millennial scheme.
glossary.text: The interpretation that Christ returns before a future earthly millennium. This companion teaches an amillennial reading. Dispensational premillennialism's separation of Israel and the church conflicts with the unity of the covenant of grace confessed in WCF 7.5 and WCF 7.6. The Westminster Standards don't name a millennial scheme.

The unfolding of God’s revealed purpose through redemptive history. Later Scripture makes earlier promises clearer and identifies their fulfillment without correcting an alleged falsehood in the earlier Word.
glossary.definition: The unfolding of God’s revealed purpose through redemptive history. Later Scripture makes earlier promises clearer and identifies their fulfillment without correcting an alleged falsehood in the earlier Word.

The pattern by which God’s spoken word in one age is brought to pass in another. The Old Testament is full of promises. The New Testament shows their fulfillment in Christ and through Him to His people.
glossary.text: The pattern by which God’s spoken word in one age is brought to pass in another. The Old Testament is full of promises. The New Testament shows their fulfillment in Christ and through Him to His people.
A passage cited as evidence for a doctrine. Its value depends upon its actual meaning and relevance. A familiar citation is not good evidence merely because it is often repeated.
glossary.definition: A passage cited as evidence for a doctrine. Its value depends upon its actual meaning and relevance. A familiar citation is not good evidence merely because it is often repeated.

The speech of God through a prophet. Prophecy in Scripture sometimes foretells future events, but as often it forth-tells the will of God for the present. Prophecy can have multiple horizons, near and far.
glossary.text: The speech of God through a prophet. Prophecy in Scripture sometimes foretells future events, but as often it forth-tells the will of God for the present. Prophecy can have multiple horizons, near and far.

glossary.definition: God’s holy, wise, and powerful preserving and governing of all His creatures and all their actions. WCF 5.
glossary.text: God’s holy, wise, and powerful preserving and governing of all His creatures and all their actions. WCF 5.

glossary.definition: The unfolding of God’s plan of salvation across the ages, from the protoevangelium of Genesis 3.15 through the cross and resurrection of Christ to His coming again. The whole Bible is redemptive history.
glossary.text: The unfolding of God’s plan of salvation across the ages, from the protoevangelium of Genesis 3.15 through the cross and resurrection of Christ to His coming again. The whole Bible is redemptive history.

glossary.definition: A theological tradition flowing from the sixteenth-century Reformation, especially through Calvin, the Puritans, and the Westminster Standards. Reformed theology emphasizes the sovereignty of God in salvation, the authority of Scripture, the regulative principle of worship, and covenant theology.
glossary.text: A theological tradition flowing from the sixteenth-century Reformation, especially through Calvin, the Puritans, and the Westminster Standards. Reformed theology emphasizes the sovereignty of God in salvation, the authority of Scripture, the regulative principle of worship, and covenant theology.

glossary.definition: The work of the Holy Spirit by which a sinner is given new spiritual life, a new heart, and a new nature. Also called the new birth. John 3.
glossary.text: The work of the Holy Spirit by which a sinner is given new spiritual life, a new heart, and a new nature. Also called the new birth. John 3.

glossary.definition: The Reformed teaching, drawn from Scripture and summarized in WCF 21.1, that the public worship of God is to be ordered only by what He has commanded in His Word, not by what He has not forbidden. Worship is the gift of God, not the invention of men. The principle guards the church from both error and presumption in approaching the Lord.
glossary.text: The Reformed teaching, drawn from Scripture and summarized in WCF 21.1, that the public worship of God is to be ordered only by what He has commanded in His Word, not by what He has not forbidden. Worship is the gift of God, not the invention of men. The principle guards the church from both error and presumption in approaching the Lord.

glossary.definition: A turning of the whole self away from sin and toward God. It's more than feeling bad. It's a change of mind, heart, and direction. Repentance begins at conversion and continues throughout the Christian life.
glossary.text: A turning of the whole self away from sin and toward God. It's more than feeling bad. It's a change of mind, heart, and direction. Repentance begins at conversion and continues throughout the Christian life.

glossary.definition: God’s making Himself known to creatures. Without revelation, creatures could not know God truly. Reformed theology distinguishes general revelation from special revelation.
glossary.text: God’s making Himself known to creatures. Without revelation, creatures could not know God truly. Reformed theology distinguishes general revelation from special revelation.

The appointed spiritual relation between a sacramental sign and the grace signified. Scripture may attribute the names or effects of one to the other without making them physically identical or the outward act automatically saving. WCF 27.2.
glossary.definition: The appointed spiritual relation between a sacramental sign and the grace signified. Scripture may attribute the names or effects of one to the other without making them physically identical or the outward act automatically saving. WCF 27.2.

The signs and seals of the covenant of grace. In the new covenant the two sacraments are baptism and the Lord’s Supper. They're means of grace by which Christ feeds and strengthens the faith of His people. WCF 27 to 29.
glossary.text: The signs and seals of the covenant of grace. In the new covenant the two sacraments are baptism and the Lord’s Supper. They're means of grace by which Christ feeds and strengthens the faith of His people. WCF 27 to 29.

glossary.definition: The lifelong work of the Holy Spirit by which believers are conformed more and more to the image of Christ, dying to sin and growing in holiness. WCF 13.
glossary.text: The lifelong work of the Holy Spirit by which believers are conformed more and more to the image of Christ, dying to sin and growing in holiness. WCF 13.

glossary.definition: The dual function of the sacraments. As a sign, the sacrament represents covenant realities to the eye. As a seal, it confirms the promises of God to the heart of the believer. WCF 27.
glossary.text: The dual function of the sacraments. As a sign, the sacrament represents covenant realities to the eye. As a seal, it confirms the promises of God to the heart of the believer. WCF 27.

glossary.definition: Latin for "Scripture alone." The Reformation conviction that the Bible alone is the supreme rule of faith and life, above all confessions, traditions, and teachers. WCF 1.10.
glossary.text: Latin for "Scripture alone." The Reformation conviction that the Bible alone is the supreme rule of faith and life, above all confessions, traditions, and teachers. WCF 1.10.

glossary.definition: The study of salvation. The whole work of God in saving sinners, from election to glorification.
glossary.text: The study of salvation. The whole work of God in saving sinners, from election to glorification.

glossary.definition: God’s revealing of Himself in Scripture and supremely in Christ. Special revelation is sufficient for salvation and for everything God requires of His people for faith and life. WCF 1.1, 1.6.
glossary.text: God’s revealing of Himself in Scripture and supremely in Christ. Special revelation is sufficient for salvation and for everything God requires of His people for faith and life. WCF 1.1, 1.6.

glossary.definition: Confessions and catechisms that summarize the teaching of Scripture. They're subordinate, meaning they sit under Scripture and are tested by it. The Westminster Standards are the subordinate standards of Reformed Presbyterian churches.
glossary.text: Confessions and catechisms that summarize the teaching of Scripture. They're subordinate, meaning they sit under Scripture and are tested by it. The Westminster Standards are the subordinate standards of Reformed Presbyterian churches.

glossary.definition: The doctrine that Christ died in the place of His people, bearing the wrath of God they deserved, so that they might receive the righteousness He earned.
glossary.text: The doctrine that Christ died in the place of His people, bearing the wrath of God they deserved, so that they might receive the righteousness He earned.
The subject, purpose, and range of a passage’s claim. Identifying scope helps us avoid making a statement answer a question it was not addressing.
glossary.definition: The subject, purpose, and range of a passage’s claim. Identifying scope helps us avoid making a statement answer a question it was not addressing.
The study of God. Properly, theology isn't just intellectual but practical, since the goal is the knowledge of God Himself in Christ.
glossary.text: The study of God. Properly, theology isn't just intellectual but practical, since the goal is the knowledge of God Himself in Christ.

glossary.definition: The doctrine that there's one God who exists eternally in three Persons: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. The three Persons are co-equal, co-eternal, and of one being. WCF 2.3.
glossary.text: The doctrine that there's one God who exists eternally in three Persons: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. The three Persons are co-equal, co-eternal, and of one being. WCF 2.3.
The completion in Christ or His saving work of a person, event, or institution appointed earlier in redemptive history. The earlier reality remains historical, while the fulfillment exceeds it.
glossary.definition: The completion in Christ or His saving work of a person, event, or institution appointed earlier in redemptive history. The earlier reality remains historical, while the fulfillment exceeds it.

A way of reading Scripture in which earlier persons, events, or institutions (the types) point forward to and are fulfilled in later realities (the antitypes), supremely in Christ. The Passover lamb is a type. Christ is the antitype.
glossary.text: A way of reading Scripture in which earlier persons, events, or institutions (the types) point forward to and are fulfilled in later realities (the antitypes), supremely in Christ. The Passover lamb is a type. Christ is the antitype.

glossary.definition: The spiritual reality by which believers are joined to Christ by the Holy Spirit, so that everything He is and has accomplished becomes ours. Justification, sanctification, adoption, and glorification all flow from union with Christ.
glossary.text: The spiritual reality by which believers are joined to Christ by the Holy Spirit, so that everything He is and has accomplished becomes ours. Justification, sanctification, adoption, and glorification all flow from union with Christ.

glossary.definition: The whole body of professing believers and their children, considered as the outward, gathered church of Christ on earth. The visible church contains both true believers and hypocrites, and is the ordinary place of grace and growth for God’s people. WCF 25.2.
glossary.text: The whole body of professing believers and their children, considered as the outward, gathered church of Christ on earth. The visible church contains both true believers and hypocrites, and is the ordinary place of grace and growth for God’s people. WCF 25.2.

glossary.definition: The Westminster Confession of Faith, the Westminster Larger Catechism, and the Westminster Shorter Catechism, all completed in the 1640s. The doctrinal standards of Reformed Presbyterian churches.
glossary.text: The Westminster Confession of Faith, the Westminster Larger Catechism, and the Westminster Shorter Catechism, all completed in the 1640s. The doctrinal standards of Reformed Presbyterian churches.

memory.html: The law of the LORD is perfect, converting the soul: the testimony of the LORD is sure, making wise the simple. The statutes of the LORD are right, rejoicing the heart: the commandment of the LORD is pure, enlightening the eyes. The fear of the LORD is clean, enduring for ever: the judgments of the LORD are true and righteous altogether. More to be desired are they than gold, yea, than much fine gold: sweeter also than honey and the honeycomb. Moreover by them is thy servant warned: and in keeping of them there is great reward.

memory.html: Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path.
memory.text: Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path.
